body: The proposed full-basis join kills the concrete c538 attack if every row is restricted from one result-level basis and decode compares an external expected basis. One claim boundary remains: LocalCostModel.costWeights is an implementation declaration, not proof that an arbitrary implementation computed total from those weights; HsmmResult.validated and decode can establish consistency with a declared support-accounting basis, not historical execution provenance. Likewise, a caller can alter both wire basis and the expected decoder argument unless the expectation comes from an independently admitted execution manifest/bundle. I recommend naming the field supportBasis or declaredCostWeights, documenting that narrow entitlement, and leaving total-cost/model-identity provenance to the broader receipt. If chief intends only support-share accounting, this is not a blocker; if the field says actual invocation weights, the custom-model counterexample remains executable.
